title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes are an attempt to build a 'tame' (modérée) topology axiomatically, in the spirit of the Esquisse d'un programme. An 'atelier' is a system of admissible 'figures' M (e.g. semi-algebraic/'special' or polyhedral figures) on a set of points L. It carries an inclusion order ≤ and a 'strictly inside' relation ≪, an analogue of 'relatively compact in the interior of'. omb(X) is the 'shadow' (point set) of a figure X, and x °≪ X means the point x is interior to X.

On p.59 Grothendieck isolates the 'quasi-ensembliste' pre-workshops: triples (M, ≤, ≪) with points L ⊂ M satisfying four axioms.
- Prat quasi 1: X ≤ Y ⇒ X ≪ Y. In context this probably means ≤ implies the weak relation; the exact form depends on his conventions.
- Prat quasi 2 (density): every figure has nonempty interior.
- Prat quasi 3 (minimal strict divisibility): if x ≪ X, there is X' ≤ X with x interior to X'.
- Prat quasi 4 (induced refinement / locality): shadows of Y and X' intersect as the union of shadows of figures below both. If Y ≤ X one may take Y' ≤ X'.
The old 'parallelism/disjointness' relation ‖ becomes superfluous once points are known: for points, x ‖ y ⇔ x ≠ y.

Page 60 is a methodological comment on this structure. If one works with points rather than with 'lieux' (point-free places, which he claims he was the first to think of), and in the setting of 'infinitely divisible' spaces (no atoms, cf. the density axiom), this small structure (M, ≤, ≪) should suffice for all needs, possibly with extra requirements added as needed. Its advantages:
- It is common to the 'special' (semi-analytic/semi-algebraic-type) and the polyhedral contexts.
- It greatly simplifies the data: only ≤ and ≪, instead of the richer data of general ateliers.
- The axioms reduce to four, 'barely more complicated than' (presumably) the axioms of a topology.

For ateliers with finite figures, the figures are already determined by the corresponding predicates. For more general special resp. polyhedral ateliers, one must add to the data a notion of '(closed) admissible part', defined by suitable local-finiteness conditions. This is the analogue of locally finite unions of figures, as in the theory of locally finite polyhedra or semianalytic sets.

A marginal note proposes renaming the interiority predicate. Instead of 'topologie' one would speak of 'Stratologie' (or 'Structologie'), stressing that the basic structure is the stratified/figure structure with an interiority predicate, not an open-set topology.

The next page builds the support/cosupport (polar) Galois closure from the disjointness relation ‖.
errors: The priority claim to be 'the first' to think of 'lieux' (point-free spaces) is historically untenable. Point-free approaches predate 1986: Whitehead/de Laguna/Tarski region-based geometry; Ehresmann's local lattices (1957); Isbell's 'locales' (1972); Johnstone's Stone Spaces (1982). Grothendieck's own topos theory (SGA4) is also point-free. He may mean his specific notion of 'lieu' within the atelier formalism.
The parenthetical claim about 'infinitely divisible' spaces versus spaces that are not, and being the first to work so, is hard to read and cannot be checked.

The page is an informal sketch. The 'local finiteness' conditions for admissible parts are announced, not given, so the sufficiency claim ('cette structure suffise à tous nos besoins') is unsubstantiated here.

ideas.what: Axiomatizing a tame topology by a set of figures with inclusion ≤ and a 'well-inside' relation ≪, plus points, with four axioms (density, divisibility, induced refinement)
ideas.modern_name: strong inclusion / proximity relation; region-based (mereotopological) theories of space; de Vries algebras; way-below relation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Efremovich (proximity, 1950s); de Vries (1962); Whitehead/de Laguna (1920s); Düntsch–Vakarelov contact algebras (2000s); o-minimal approach for tame topology (van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight 1980s)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology is announced in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), but the atelier/≪ axiomatics appears only in these unpublished notes

ideas.what: A single structure common to the semi-analytic ('spécial') and polyhedral (PL) contexts
ideas.modern_name: uniform axiomatic setting for o-minimal / PL / semialgebraic categories
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimality (van den Dries, Pillay, Steinhorn, Knight, 1984–86) plays this role in the literature
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 discusses the goal in general terms

ideas.what: Passing from finite figures to general ateliers via 'admissible' parts defined by local finiteness
ideas.modern_name: locally finite unions; G-topology / admissible coverings (as in rigid geometry)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tate/Kiehl (admissible coverings), classical PL topology (locally finite complexes)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's reduction of tame topology to a structure (M, ≤, ≪) on figures with points, together with the disjointness relation ‖ and polar closure on p.61, is essentially a region-based/mereotopological theory of space (contact/proximity algebras with a well-inside relation). It is aimed at tame (semialgebraic/PL) geometry. The literature on contact algebras and region-based theories, and the literature on o-minimal tame topology, have not, as far as I know, been connected through this kind of axiomatics.
missed.quote: il semblerait que cette structure suffise à tous nos besoins ... Cette structure a l'avantage d'être commune aux contextes "spéciaux" et "polyédral"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This could suggest a point-light, order-theoretic axiomatization of tame topology parallel to o-minimality. It links mereotopology (qualitative spatial reasoning, de Vries duality) with semialgebraic/PL geometry.

missed.claim: Local-finiteness conditions defining 'admissible' parts for general (non-finite) special/polyhedral ateliers are announced but not formulated on this page.
missed.quote: il faut introduire dans les données la notion de partie (fermée) "admissible" par des conditions convenables de "locale finitude"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is needed for any non-compact version of the theory, analogous to admissible coverings in rigid geometry or locally finite triangulations.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is mostly methodological commentary. It is interesting as evidence that Grothendieck's tame-topology program went toward a mereotopological 'well-inside' axiomatics rather than o-minimality, and for the 'Stratologie' coinage. No finished result appears here, and the priority claims are doubtful.
transcription_corrections: 'aux contextes "affines" et "polyédral"' should likely read 'aux contextes "spéciaux" et "polyédral"' (matching the 'ensembliste spéciaux' of p.59)
'ateliers généraux {+affinoïdes+} resp. polyédraux' likely reads 'ateliers (spéciaux resp. polyédraux) plus généraux'
'réduits ici au rôle de quatre' likely 'réduites ici au nombre de quatre' (the four Prat quasi axioms)
'peine plus compliqué que' likely 'à peine plus compliquées que' (the axioms of a topology, presumably)
'et non lisses[?]' is uncertain; the passage concerns spaces that are or are not 'infiniment divisibles'
Margin: reads roughly 'En introduisant pour le prédicat d'intériorité ... p.ex. "Stratologie" ou "Structologie" (au lieu de "topologie"!)'
'(ou plus exactement)' is an insertion qualifying 'ateliers à figures finies'
